children: secured a U.S. Army contract valued at up to $1.2 billion for the next version of its Precision Strike Missile, moving the program toward production after recent flight testing.

The indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity agreement covers initial purchases, additional orders and continued development of the PrSM Increment 2. Lockheed Martin said the award also supports work across its U.S. manufacturing network.

The missile completed its second flight test in August after an earlier test in March. The latest test demonstrated the system's ability to engage a moving maritime target, while Increment 2 includes a multimode seeker designed for moving land and sea targets. Additional flight testing is planned for 2027.

Lockheed Martin is also expanding manufacturing capacity as the Army prepares for larger PrSM purchases. The company has said its broader production plan aims to quadruple output, adding capacity while development of later missile variants continues.

title: A  $1.2 Billion Why Lockheed Martin In Focus
